items.title: Show HN: I'm 16 y/o and Built the only AI Agent for Hardware and Software Dev
items.why_it_matters: A 16-year-old developer just shipped Sprocket, an open-source AI agent designed for hardware and software development. Seeing someone younger than you ship a functional agent codebase is highly motivating. You can clone their repository this week to study how they structured their agent's file-handling logic and apply those patterns to your own AI-ingest tool.

items.title: Show HN: LLM Tools that I made that I cant live without
items.why_it_matters: An indie developer shipped 0verload, a tool that automatically tracks micro-versions of your source code between Git commits, specifically designed to prevent LLMs from overwriting your hard work. This directly solves the vibe-coding pain point of Claude deleting working code. You can install it this week to auto-save your Next.js files while Claude Code runs, giving you an instant safety net to revert to if a prompt goes sideways.

items.title: Show HN: Nuking the crap Claude left in the codebase – CCN
items.why_it_matters: A developer shipped CCN, a lightweight tool that safely strips out the excessive, redundant comments that Claude and other LLMs frequently inject into your codebase. Since AI-generated comments can quickly clutter your Next.js project, you can run this tool on your AI-ingest repository this week to clean up your codebase before your next Git commit.

items.title: Show HN: Galda – Come back to Claude Code/Codex without digging through Git
items.why_it_matters: Galda is a new tool designed to help you jump back into your Claude Code and Codex sessions without having to dig through your Git history to figure out what changed. This makes managing your AI-assisted development sessions much cleaner. You can sign up for the beta this week to track your next building session on AI-ingest.

items.title: Anthropic's Fever Dream: Claude's package that stole real keys
items.why_it_matters: A security analysis revealed a rogue package incident where compromised dependencies could potentially steal API keys during autonomous agent execution. Since you use Claude Code and external APIs daily, you should audit your AI-ingest package.json and environment variables this week to ensure your Supabase and Anthropic keys are securely stored and not exposed to untrusted third-party scripts.

items.title: Claude for ADHD: The Coding Workflow I Built for My Brain
items.why_it_matters: A developer shared their custom Claude Code workflow tailored for staying focused and managing cognitive load during long coding sessions. It contains practical tips on structuring terminal commands and managing context. You can adopt their 'one-task-at-a-time' prompt template this week to keep your Claude Code sessions focused on shipping single features for AI-ingest.

items.title: Show HN: Claude Code takes forever, so I filled the waiting with Pokémon
items.why_it_matters: A developer built Claudemon, a CLI tool that spawns wild Pokémon in your terminal to keep you entertained while waiting for Claude Code to finish generating large blocks of code. You can install this npm package this week to make the waiting periods during your next AI-ingest build session a bit more fun.

items.title: Gauge – see where your Claude Code subscription goes
items.why_it_matters: Gauge is a new open-source tool that helps you visualize and track exactly where your Claude Code subscription and token usage are going. You can clone this repository this week and run it locally to see which of your recent AI-ingest prompts consumed the most tokens, helping you optimize your future queries.
